chapter: Arranging for Fletcher, Goodman and Barnet
title: Chicago in the thirties: the 400 and 5100 Clubs, Ray Nance leaves for Ellington
summary: Clarifies he went with Fletcher to Chicago, left to form his own band at Swingland, then returned. At the 5100 Club with Danny Thomas on the bill, violinist-trumpeter Ray Nance was persuaded to join Duke Ellington.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I'm trying to note here -- after you had been -- after you left school and went to New York and then we got into talking about Chicago, about when was it that you went to Chicago and spent a lot of time there? Was that the late twenties or --

No, this was in the thirties. You know, Fletcher went to Chicago. In fact, he took his band into Chicago where and this was when I was with Fletcher, and I stayed with Fletcher, I believe, better than a year in Chicago, and this is when I formed my own band and went into Swingland, and Fletcher was at the Grand Terrace.
You had been with Fletcher first, and then formed your band, or you had your band first and then you went with Fletcher?
Well, both. I was with him first, and then I had my band for a while.
And then you went back with him.
And then I went back with Fletcher. Yes. But those days in Chicago were the Thirties.
Is this when the so-called Chicago style was really getting itself together with --
This was when I had the pleasure of playing the 400 Club when I had personnel with me like Ray
Nance -- Ray Nance just before he joined Duke. I was playing the 5100 Club, and one of the performers that was on that show was the great Danny Thomas.
Oh yeah. You just started to talk about Danny Thomas.

Oh yes. That was in the 5100 Club in Chicago, and I had a big band then. There was a fellow there that played the violin and the trumpet. And his name was Ray Nance. He was quite an inspiration to us, and he was always a salesman. A Chicago boy. And Duke Ellington came to town and heard Ray. (Inaudible). He loved Ray and wanted Ray to join him. You know, Ray didn't want to leave the band? He wanted to stay with us, and I had to get mad with Ray. Ray will tell anybody this, and finally, we showed him where it would be a great advantage, and one of those things, and he joined Duke, and you know the story from there on. This was in the 5100 Club in the Thirties, and there was some other things that happened there in Chicago.
